draft.title: Internal migration in China
card: Since about 1980, hundreds of millions of people in China have moved from the countryside to cities. This is internal migration, because they stay inside China. It is one of the largest migrations in history.
Many moved to find work in factories and in service jobs, such as shops, restaurants and building sites. Wages in cities were often higher than farm incomes. These are pull factors.
The hukou is China's household registration system. It records where a family is officially registered, and access to services such as public schools and health care has often depended on that place.
Many rural migrants have worked in cities without a city hukou. This has made it harder for them to use city services, and some have left children with relatives in their home village.
draft.remember: Rural Chinese moved to cities for work, and the hukou system shaped what services they could use there.

opts: A household registration system tied to a place
A government program that builds new factory towns
A rule that bans people from leaving their country
A tax paid by workers who move to a city
a.why: The hukou records where a family is officially registered, and services have often depended on that place. It does not build towns, ban travel or collect a tax.
a.clue: Think about what it records about a family.

b.q: Wei moves from a farming village to a city factory in China. He keeps his village hukou, and his daughter cannot easily enrol in a city public school. What does this show?
opts: The hukou can limit migrants' access to city services
Wei has made an international move between countries
Wei has moved because of a push factor only
Cities in China do not need factory workers
b.why: Services such as public schools have often depended on the place of registration, so a village hukou can limit access in the city. Wei stays inside China, so his move is not international.
b.clue: Which option links the school problem to where he is registered?

a.best: A household registration system tied to a place

b.best: The hukou can limit migrants' access to city services
